set.body:
Current implementation boundary

Sequential assessment 2026-09-12: retain P1, refine around adopted estimate artifacts rather than a second receipt hierarchy. Current FitEstimateProducer writes OLS estimator/noise/nuisance/run-combination provenance and scalar residual df. estimates.Products already has DfRole/DfValue/DegreesOfFreedom including approximate and unknown representations. EstimateGroup retains pinned inputs in GroupEstimateBlock, validates product/observation/target/pooling alignment and independent participant identities, and requires GroupEstimateAdmission.verify(units). This is substantial existing provenance support, not complete scientific admission. GroupData itself still contains effects/variances without first-level uncertainty semantics; the eager former FirstLevel.groupData is now FitGroupAdapter.groupData and still squares SEs without carrying df. Its meta-analysis-ready documentation must not be interpreted as calibrated inference admission. Remaining work: use the existing artifact/admission seam to bind and validate known/estimated/approximate/unknown uncertainty and sample-dependent df, qualify GLS and run-pooled producer receipts, define the eager bridge policy, and test subject/sample reorder, geometry evidence and refusals. Provenance is not calibration; retain independent numerical acceptance and do not invent effective df. Source-only assessment; no new inference admission or runtime qualification.

Original scientific requirements and historical evidence

GroupData currently retains per-subject effects and variances but not the origin, residual/effective degrees of freedom, serial-noise treatment or combination history of that uncertainty. FirstLevel.groupData squares SEs from TContrastResult and drops its df; voxel indices alone do not prove geometry/co-registration. This is a native scientific-admission boundary, not an application-local metadata patch.

Implement a typed subject/contrast/sample-bound uncertainty receipt distinguishing known variance, estimated variance with supported df, approximate effective df, and unknown provenance; retain estimator, serial correlation policy, run combination and explicit geometry/registration evidence where actually available. Do not invent df, assume independent contrasts/FIR bins or conflate descriptive SEs with a symmetry assumption. Preserve current EffectsOnly capability and total rejection of invalid uncertainty. Scalar df should stay compact when shared; per-sample df must align to the sample axis. Reference first-level run pooling behavior rather than deriving a new application fitter.

Acceptance: real first-level-to-group bridge regressions with voxel and subject reorderings, named contrast consistency, pooled-run uncertainty, missing/unknown receipts, invalid df and geometry mismatch; JVM/JS portable contracts and workflow-consumer evidence. Link the first-level GLS qualification ticket bd-01M1Z2050HGVC8FAZM07TM2K9Q where it supplies policy evidence. Supports group-inference admission bd-01M20TKX7VYFT3BHCM7QAMA6NG and manifest-backed execution bd-01KX6G9BFJRERNFRWR17WT0YGN. Do not hold up the bounded equal-subject symmetry primitive by claiming it mathematically requires SE or df.
